### 1. Codex Model Router Optimization v3.0.1

Status: **downloaded**. Inspection: **all 69 supplied release members fully read**, coverage receipts reconciled, extracted bytes match original ZIP, CRC valid (October 6, 2026). Runtime: **not installed or tested**. Latest upstream release/current compatibility unverified.
Purpose and type: Executable Python tooling plus agent contracts and skill. One writer, independent reviewer, versioned JSON packets, session observations and worktree snapshots. Static inspection only; runtime untested.
Lesson: [Skool source](https://www.skool.com/aimoney/classroom/be6b9963?md=3dc80c2509c8438b829f0da87f6f25d8)
File source: [exact download](https://github.com/jeffjhunter/codex-model-router-optimization/releases/download/v3.0.1/codex-model-router-optimization-3.0.1.zip)
Local ZIP: [codex-model-router-optimization-3.0.1.zip](/Users/alexlobaito/Documents/Codex/2026-10-06/can/outputs/agent-packages/codex-model-router-optimization-3.0.1.zip)
Extracted entries: 69. SHA-256: `c38d5c8859d9fc25738e397d154bd05dce08c74d389df4ef67ff8e9e0767ebc1`.

**Source inspection, October 6, 2026 — session identity and installation writes:** The full `observe_session.py` implements local Codex JSONL observation rather than accepting the worker's model claim. It extracts session metadata, task-start markers and turn contexts; checks supplied expected model, effort, workspace, turn and parent; refuses ambiguous matching logs; and requires a specific expected turn for forked sessions so inherited context cannot stand in for the new turn. It outputs metadata without message/tool contents, although workspace/source paths remain visible. This establishes implemented identity-check logic, not tested runtime behavior or task-result truth. Without optional expectations, its “verified” label means a model-bearing turn context was found, not that a required model was matched.

The installer's `AtomicBatch` stages and fsyncs file bytes, replaces destinations with temporary backups and attempts rollback on exceptions. It explicitly describes itself as best-effort. The inspected class has no persistent recovery journal, agent checkpoint or resume mechanism; a process interruption is not handled by ordinary Python exception rollback (inference from the source). Ranking remains high for reusable identity/verification tooling; shared memory and durable workflow recovery are not supplied by these two components. [Exact scope and hashes](/Users/alexlobaito/Documents/Codex/2026-10-06/can/work/router-observer-source-inspection.json). No installer or tests executed.


**Reporting and collision checks — full static inspection of packet validator, worktree snapshot and protocol, October 6, 2026:**

- **Handoff mechanism:** raw JSON worker and reviewer packets with run ID, plan version, actor identity, criteria and evidence. A separate authoritative context can bind the run/plan/actor/model, expected acceptance IDs, worker attempt and allowed file paths. The Python validator checks these matches and rejects unsafe paths or reported changes outside scope. Context is optional at CLI level; without it, validation only checks the packet’s intrinsic shape/consistency. Actual filesystem changes are not compared with the report by this validator.
- **Completion gate:** reviewer acceptance requires every criterion and verification result to pass, at least one verification, and no findings/blockers. Worker `done` by itself does not require all criteria to pass. Evidence is validated as nonempty text; the script does not run commands or inspect evidence artifacts. A plausible false report can satisfy those text checks (inference), so schema validity is not task truth.
- **Collision detection:** `snapshot_worktree.py` hashes the Git index, status and tracked/nonignored untracked file contents, modes and symlink targets. It detects net before/after differences when the coordinator takes both snapshots. It does not prevent writes, implement leases/locks, copy file contents or restore state. Ignored files and nested submodule contents are excluded. Per-file size/mtime checks catch some concurrent changes during hashing; no globally atomic multi-file snapshot is established. Output includes the absolute repository root despite the docstring’s never-paths statement.
- **Controller boundary:** protocol.md explicitly says native Codex does not enforce a state machine. Its coordinator rules require independent observations, packet validation and root-owned snapshots; these are written operating requirements around executable helper scripts. No durable controller, shared database or memory service is established by these inspected files. Hardcoded validator routes use GPT-5.6 model IDs; current compatibility is untested.

Ranking: high for inspectable reporting contracts and verification helpers, with runtime proof still absent. [Full inspected-file scope and hashes](/Users/alexlobaito/Documents/Codex/2026-10-06/can/work/router-contract-source-inspection.json). No downloaded scripts or tests executed.


**Final gate and agent profiles — October 6, 2026:** Fully read `validate_run.py` and the Luna/Terra/Sol TOML profiles. Complete final records require distinct coordinator/worker/reviewer task identities and observed turns, recorded stock model identities, true pin/observation flags, one to three implementation attempts, passing requirement entries and no blockers. Explicit accounting separates implementation/review turns from format-only repairs, allows at most one repair per invalid action packet, and requires each review action to have matching before/after worktree digests. Legacy v3 turn accounting is also accepted.

This final validator intentionally reads sanitized JSON only: it does not reopen session logs, recompute snapshots, authenticate observation flags or bind the listed requirements to a separately supplied original plan. Its pass establishes record consistency, not independent execution proof or original-scope completeness. Writer profiles configure `workspace-write`; the reviewer configures `read-only` and written restrictions against changes. The reviewer instructions acknowledge that parent runtime overrides can supersede sandbox defaults, so this is a declared configuration boundary rather than proven universal isolation. These profiles contain no fleet-wide mailbox, shared memory backend or distributed writer lease. [Four-file full-read receipt](/Users/alexlobaito/Documents/Codex/2026-10-06/can/work/router-final-gate-source-inspection.json). Runtime remains untested; no downloaded code executed.

- S5 P3 requires **50 test support tickets**, accuracy/tone/helpfulness scored separately, target average 8+/10; explicitly verify escalation delivery, human notification, context passing and response-time commitments. Written test protocol, no fixtures or test runner provided.
- S5 P4 calls for a limited initial launch with **100% response review**, daily adjustments, then metrics for handled/escalated share, satisfaction and response time, with weekly knowledge-base updates. S8 P4 similarly requires review of every automated action during the initial launch.
- S8 P2 gives a community moderator prompt and human mention escalation; S8 P3 organizes topical community channels. This is agent-to-human moderation, not an inter-agent communication contract or collision-control design.

Provisional value: the testing and escalation checklist is reusable, but this section ranks below the downloaded validators and Power User Kit. Marketing, content and pricing examples excluded from agent infrastructure recommendations. No runtime demonstrated by this text scan.

This reduces damage from failed source resolution; it does not establish atomic or crash-safe replacement.

- **Viewer:** source config includes sample status, IDs, input, scores, tokens, duration and explanation/highlights. It assigns lower-is-better to most behavior scores and higher-is-better to realism. It is a display configuration around Inspect, not independent verification of facts.

## Persona OS operating protocols and package gaps — October 6, 2026

**Progress:** eleven operating/reference files fully read in this batch; TEAM.md upgraded from partial to full inspection. Changelog opening release sections inspected; the full changelog and other package members remain pending. Source package v2.0.0, May 19, 2026; no installation or execution. [Inspection receipt](/Users/alexlobaito/Documents/Codex/2026-10-06/can/work/persona-os-operating-protocol-inspection.json).

**Communication and ownership:** TEAM-template.md supplies role, reports-to, responsibilities, contact reason and Discord/Slack member IDs, with priority channels and confidentiality levels. AGENTS-template.md requires direct mention/address or a one-to-one DM before engagement and proposes host `requireMention` enforcement. These are useful written routing rules; they do not implement a job assignment protocol, acknowledgments, result mailbox, leases or concurrent file-write protection. ESCALATION-template.md explicitly hands off to the human with goal, attempted approaches/results, blocker, specific ask, suggested next action and delay impact. It supplies no executable agent-to-agent messaging or evidence verifier.

**Recovery:** never-forget-protocol.md plus checkpoint/daily-log templates include decisions with reasoning, owners, current status, resume steps and pre-operation success/failure steps. This is a more useful recovery record than a bare conversation summary, but relies on the agent writing and reading it. Claimed 95% recovery remains unmeasured. WORKFLOWS-template.md adds outcome journaling and promotion after repeated practice; it is an initially empty process template, not an orchestrator.

**Important shared-memory distinction:** SECURITY_NOTE.md line 46 names `~/.openclaw/memory/<agentId>.sqlite` as the host index. That is an author claim about a per-agent index; it does not describe a central index accessible to every runtime. It strengthens the requirement to inspect actual shared-source configuration rather than treating SQLite as fleet sharing. No SQL schema, replication, shared retrieval endpoint or access configuration supplied here.

**Static package inconsistencies, not runtime test failures:**

- `references/heartbeat-automation.md` lines 405/417 requires `scripts/config-validator.sh`; no such member exists in the verified 69-file archive. Line 161 optionally names health-check.sh, also absent. Cannot rank a missing validator as supplied working code.
- Guide lines 159/181 embed shell date substitution inside double-quoted scheduled-job message arguments. By shell semantics, these examples resolve the date when the job is registered rather than when it later runs (inference from the written command). The separately supplied cron .sh files instead use “today’s log” wording; those do not contain this date substitution.
- Guide says isolated jobs make no network calls while its briefing requests channel scans and announcements. Isolation alone does not establish network prohibition; behavior was not tested.
- HEARTBEAT-template.md archives overflow facts before retaining current ones; SKILL.md maintenance instructs pruning old entries in place. Preserve both as conflicting guidance rather than claiming a uniformly safe retention policy.
- Main skill describes per-agent workspace overrides; the fully read resolve-workspace.sh checks environment/default workspace but not `agents.list[].workspace`. Multi-agent helpers cannot be assumed to resolve the active agent’s overridden workspace.

**Ranking update:** high-value written package for agent identity, checkpoint formats and structured reporting; medium as automation scaffolding; not a supplied shared-memory service or durable multi-agent orchestrator. Its contact/mention rules can reduce unwanted chat replies, but do not prevent two assigned agents from changing the same resource. No templates adopted into live agents. Whole resource search remains active.

**User requirement:** automatic extraction and retrieval, persistent across sessions, with one shared knowledge store accessible to the agent fleet. This batch verifies the strongest existing lead rather than treating instruction files as a complete memory service.

**Live instructor source:** [Openclaw lost its memory](https://www.skool.com/aimoney/openclaw-lost-its-memory), Jeff J Hunter reply, Mar 16 UI; year not displayed. Full post and sole reply opened and expanded on October 6, 2026. Jeff describes pre-compaction memoryFlush, daily disk notes and session-end summaries, then explicitly recommends the openclaw-mem0 plugin for memory outside the context window. His claim that this prevents all future memory loss is not established by that discussion; no shared-fleet implementation, working backend configuration or runtime receipt is attached. The 2026 dates inside his example are not proof of the post year.

**Publisher sources freshly refreshed:** [Hermes integration](https://docs.mem0.ai/integrations/hermes) and [OpenClaw integration](https://docs.mem0.ai/integrations/openclaw), October 6, 2026; publisher dates unknown. OpenClaw page identifies package version 1.1.0.

| Required behavior | Documented mechanism | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|
| Automatic extraction | Hermes background extraction after each turn; OpenClaw triage and automatic capture | Hermes messages capped at 450 characters by default; overlapping capture may be skipped |
| Automatic retrieval | Relevant memories injected before the next turn | Hermes waits up to three seconds and can proceed without recall |
| Persistent shared storage | Mem0 Cloud, self-hosted HTTP server, Qdrant server or PostgreSQL/pgvector | No Alex-agent backend inspected or configured in this research |
| Shared access across agents | Stable user identity controls memory namespace; Hermes writes carry agent/channel metadata | Common backend/namespace is an architectural inference; cross-platform interoperability untested |
| Worker contributions | OpenClaw subagents can recall parent memories | Publisher explicitly says their sessions are not captured |
| Reliable capture through interruption | Hermes graceful shutdown waits for workers | Publisher explicitly says no durable queue; forced exit can interrupt writes |

**Architecture implication (inference):** the documented server route is a candidate for several separate agents accessing shared knowledge. Concurrent separate Hermes processes should use a server rather than opening the same local Qdrant directory. Sharing knowledge does not itself supply task ownership, collision avoidance or verified completion receipts. Those remain separate Observatory requirements.

**Concrete acceptance still outstanding:** agent A learns a distinctive fact through ordinary conversation; A exits; independently started agent B retrieves it without copied conversation history; repeat for a worker-produced fact; demonstrate observable capture failure and restart behavior. No runtime test, installation, credentials, profile edit or external write performed. This is researched and documented, not set up or seen working.

## What we actually have

We have substantial pieces of an agent build and harness: role templates, host provisioning code, skills, task contracts, handoff packets, observation helpers and review procedures. We do not have a complete demonstrated Jeff fleet deployment combining shared memory, durable task ownership, agent transport, recovery and independent verification.

This document selects the strongest inspected pieces and describes the missing connections. It is a synthesis for building the system, not a claim that Jeff supplied every component. The [canonical inventory](ai-money-agent-file-inventory.md) remains the authority for downloads, full source links, hashes, inspection scope and inaccessible resources. This document is the authority for the proposed build, avoiding another duplicate inventory.

- **AI MONEY:** instructor statement or course-supplied artifact.
- **VENDOR:** publisher documentation, independently of Jeff.
- **PROPOSED:** our adaptation/design, not found as a completed course deployment.
- **NOT PROVEN:** no live receipt establishing the behavior.

“Best” here means strongest fit among inspected material for Alex's requirements. We have not benchmarked these packages or established the latest versions globally. ## Recommended build shape

**PROPOSED:** retain the agent runtime as the worker; put durable task state and evidence outside the conversation. Use course contracts for the controller/worker/reviewer relationship, Mem0 as a candidate knowledge layer, and Observatory for inspectable state and evidence. This extends the course material where necessary.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Alex / authorized request] --> C[Controller: freezes scope and acceptance]
    C --> T[Durable task and event store]
    T --> W[Worker: isolated role and workspace]
    W --> E[Artifact and evidence store]
    W --> T
    T --> V[Independent verifier]
    E --> V
    V --> T
    T --> O[Observatory: current state and history]
    E --> O
    W <--> M[Shared Mem0 service]
    C <--> M
    V <--> M
```

The professional engineering criteria for this proposal are transactional task ownership, at-least-once delivery with idempotent handling, independent verification, and restart recovery from persisted state. These are proposed design criteria, not a certification or claim about the downloaded packages. Their failure cases are defined below.

## 3. Harness: controller, worker and verifier

A harness is the code and operating rules around the model: task dispatch, tool execution, state, retries, logging and completion checks.

**AI MONEY assets:** [Codex Model Router v3.0.1](agent-packages/codex-model-router-optimization-3.0.1), dated July 14, 2026, and [Claude Smart Orchestrator v2.1.3](agent-packages/Claude-Code-Smart-Orchestrator-Giveaway-v2.1.3), release day unverified. Both contain code and contracts; neither was executed here. Use the package suited to the coding runtime, not two conflicting coordinators over one task.

**PROPOSED roles:** controller owns scope and task transitions; worker creates outputs; independent verifier evaluates the original acceptance criteria and actual artifacts. For the first proof, one controller, one worker and one verifier are enough. Concurrent unrelated work can be added after recovery works.

Use the [plan packet example](agent-packages/codex-model-router-optimization-3.0.1/codex-model-router-optimization-3.0.1/examples/plan-packet.yaml) to carry run ID, plan version, requirement IDs, acceptance IDs, allowed files, baseline, prohibited actions and actor identities. Attach outputs, commands/results, source dates and remaining blockers to the return packet.

**Limitation:** packet validators check structure and consistency. They do not independently execute commands, prove evidence truthful or compare every claimed output with reality. Optional authoritative context must become required in our adaptation. Runtime/model IDs need compatibility review.

## 4. Communication and exclusive task ownership

**AI MONEY assets:** [Provider-Proof handoff templates](agent-packages/provider-proof-ai-workflow-kit-complete/Provider-Proof-Agentic-AI-Workflow-Kit-Package/03-Templates/03-Portable-Handoff-Packet-Template), publication date unknown; Power User Kit portable-context guidance. They provide useful payloads, not a durable transport.

**PROPOSED, missing implementation:** one durable task service stores assignments/results. Agents communicate with that service through authenticated APIs/tools. Slack/Discord/Telegram can notify or receive requests; the persisted record determines ownership and completion.

Minimum objects: agents, tasks, attempts, task events, messages, artifacts, verification receipts and memory-capture jobs. Each task carries mission/client boundary, request version, acceptance criteria, owner, status, lease expiry and monotonically increasing ownership generation. Each message has a unique ID and references its task/attempt.

Claim work in one transaction. Renew a time-limited claim while working. Reject writes/results from an expired ownership generation. Deduplicate retried messages. Persist state changes and outgoing notifications together, then deliver notifications with retries. Keep failed deliveries visible. Exact database/schema/API implementation is not supplied by the course; database deployment choice remains open.

**Collision rules:** exclusive ownership for one task; isolated workspaces for writers; explicit ownership of shared external records; serialize conflicting edits. Host isolation alone cannot protect two agents editing the same CRM record.

**Acceptance:** two workers try the same task; only one gets the active claim. After expiry and reassignment, the old worker's completion is rejected. Duplicate result delivery produces one effective completion. Retried external effects use an idempotency mechanism or require reconciliation before repetition.

## 5. Persistent shared knowledge

**AI MONEY:** Jeff recommends Mem0 in the March 16 reply and describes shared Obsidian context separately. Do not claim these form a demonstrated single pipeline.

**VENDOR:** [Hermes Mem0 documentation](https://docs.mem0.ai/integrations/hermes) and [OpenClaw integration](https://docs.mem0.ai/integrations/openclaw), checked October 6, 2026; OpenClaw page declares plugin 1.1.0. Hermes documents per-turn recall and background extraction, with Cloud or self-hosted HTTP/storage options. Compatible host/plugin migration must be checked before installation.

**PROPOSED candidate:** one Mem0 server for the pilot, shared deliberately scoped knowledge identity, separate agent IDs on writes. Knowledge scopes must preserve mission/client boundaries. Use agent-local instructions for role behavior and the task store for ownership/status; extracted conversational facts cannot declare a task verified.

Hermes profile connection is in its active home's mem0.json; it specifies provider mode, endpoint and memory identity. Multi-process local-directory sharing is not the documented route; use a server. Cross-platform Hermes/OpenClaw namespace compatibility remains untested. Do not apply one global namespace to all client material blindly.

**Known gaps:** Hermes capture defaults to 450 characters per message, can skip overlapping turns and has no durable capture queue. OpenClaw subagents recall parent memories but their sessions are not automatically captured. Auto-capture versus session/long-term promotion needs explicit testing.

**PROPOSED extension:** durable capture jobs with source/task/agent identity, retries, visible failures and deduplication. Automatically route worker findings through the same capture path. Retrieval should preserve original evidence pointers and dates; a remembered assertion is not proof of truth. This extension is not delivered in the inspected Mem0 package.

**Acceptance:** A learns a unique fact through ordinary conversation; A exits; separately started B recalls it without copied history. Repeat with a worker-created fact and within two distinct project scopes. Verify isolation. Interrupt capture/backend connectivity; inspect loss/retry behavior rather than relying on a status command.

## 6. Checkpoints and restart recovery

**AI MONEY:** daily checkpoint/recovery templates and the Power User Kit. **PROPOSED:** add a persisted machine-readable checkpoint linked to task/attempt and artifact hashes. Record finished steps, unresolved work, last observed results, side effects already performed and next permissible action.

After restart, reload task state, the original acceptance criteria, latest valid checkpoint and artifacts. Reconcile uncertain external effects before retrying. Preserve attempts and failures rather than overwriting them with a success message. Reclaim expired work through the task service.

**Acceptance:** stop a worker after creating an artifact but before reporting. A fresh worker recovers the artifact and task state, verifies whether the action already happened, and finishes once. An interrupted installer checkpoint is not equivalent to this workflow recovery.

## 7. Evidence, monitoring and Observatory

**AI MONEY assets:** Power User Kit evidence requirements; router session observer/worktree snapshots; Claude trace verifiers. These help check identities, lifecycle and changed files. They cannot alone establish business-output correctness.

**PROPOSED Observatory views:** queued/running/awaiting review/verified/blocked/failed work; owner and lease; attempts and last heartbeat; artifacts; independent checks; delivery/capture failures; chronological event history. Current state is a projection of persisted events, rebuilt and reconciled after restart.

Only the verifier can promote an output to verified, using original criteria and its own observations. Store exact observed commands/results or application readbacks, artifact hashes and checker identity/version. Distinguish configured, synthetic success and real runtime success. Contradictory evidence blocks acceptance. No design can guarantee an agent never lies; the goal is to detect unsupported claims and prevent them from changing authoritative state.

**Acceptance:** worker returns a plausible false success packet; syntax validation passes but independent artifact checking rejects it. Stale/missing evidence cannot pass. A restarted Observatory rebuilds the same current task state from saved history.

## Build sequence and exit checks

1. **Recover existing state:** inventory actual agents, hosts, runtimes, Observatory storage and permissions. Identify what already works; avoid duplicate infrastructure. Output a current-state receipt. Not done by this document.
2. **One complete task:** adapt one contract, isolated worker workspace and independent review; save request/output/checks outside chat. Deliberately false report must fail.
3. **Durable ownership and handoff:** implement transactional claims, message/result deduplication and replayable state. Race and stale-owner checks must pass.
4. **Recovery:** interrupt the task at meaningful boundaries, restart with a fresh process and reconcile side effects. No silently duplicated action.
5. **Shared memory:** connect two agents to one scoped backend; prove automatic learning, cross-session recall and worker contributions. Record capture failures.
6. **Observatory readback:** show actual persisted task/events/artifacts/receipts and memory failures; rebuild after restart.
7. **Expand by role:** add skills/agents only after the same acceptance checks apply to them. Multi-agent business effects need their own live readbacks.

A. Explicit OpenClaw → Claude Code instructions

### A. Explicit OpenClaw → Claude Code instructions

Jeff's [Have OpenClaw use Claude Code on the same VPS](https://www.skool.com/aimoney/have-openclaw-use-claude-code-on-same-vps) post gives a concrete route. UI date **April 4, edited; year not displayed**. Full post and three comment entries were inspected previously; the saved inline reference was fully reread October 7.

1. OpenClaw turns the user's request into a clear brief with the goal, existing files and project directory.
2. It starts Claude Code through the **local CLI process** on the same host. This particular guide instructs that route rather than ACP/sessions_spawn for Claude Code; it is not a universal statement about every available harness.
3. Longer jobs run in the background; the parent monitors process logs. Small jobs run in the foreground and return directly.
4. The worker brief includes an instruction to run `openclaw system event --text 'Done: [brief summary]' --mode now` when finished. The stated purpose is waking the parent so it can report without the user asking.
5. The parent reports plainly and starts another Claude Code job with revision instructions when needed.

The guide's default project organization is `~/.openclaw/workspace/projects/` with separate project folders. That is directory organization, not a task lock. Its historical command contains a permission-bypass option; it was preserved as source material and was not executed or adopted.

Our adaptation of the acquisition prompt and Prospect Finder evidence rules, not Jeff's exact wording or shipped large-scale workflow:

Process this contact list for [offer] and [buyer criteria]. Use only the supplied contact fields and retrieved website evidence. ## Topic lookup and recall — SKILL.md lines836–873

`MEMORY.md` and the `memory/` directory are indexed by OpenClaw's built-in memory engine. Prefer `memory_get` over `exec: cat` for these files — it reads from the index, avoids re-reading on every call, and is the canonical 5.x pattern:

```
memory_get: <WORKSPACE>/MEMORY.md
```

For a topic-level lookup ("what did we decide about pricing?"), use `memory_search` instead — it does hybrid keyword+vector search across all indexed memory files:

```
memory_search: "pricing decisions Q1"
```

# Jev, Clef, and CRM contact grading

Research reference and proposed implementation guide  
Research checked: October 7, 2026  
Status: sources and example request checked; no live integration, inference, deployment, or customer contact performed

## 1. Main finding

Jev and Cloudflare’s Clef are decision models. They evaluate supplied information against questions with defined answers and return structured values and probabilities. They can classify a contact, score documented customer fit, identify buying intent, select a supported outreach angle, or flag a draft for review.

The clearest sales implementation found was an agency using Jev to score opportunities and show a review card to its team. The same agency reports using Jev to select evidence-backed outreach angles. Neither report establishes an increase in hires, replies, meetings, or revenue. No named Clef sales deployment with measured sales outcomes was verified.

For a CRM with existing contacts, the recommended first application is **contact grading and review prioritization**. Read the contact’s relevant facts and conversation history, evaluate several questions, and save the assessment in dedicated fields. A salesperson reviews the prioritized list. A separate generative model could later draft replies using the classifications.

That recommendation is an inference from the practitioner reports, the documented classification architecture, and the missed candidates in a published lead-scoring test. It is not a deployment already running in Alex’s CRM.

| Choice | Select one supplied option, with probabilities and confidence | Pricing request, booking request, objection, later, or unclear |
| Score | Evaluate against ordered descriptions; return a probability-weighted score | General curiosity through active vendor evaluation |
| Noul | Return the probability that a yes/no statement is true | Does this message request a human? |

Jev currently accepts text, JSON objects, and arrays of text. It does not write messages, generate code, explain its reasoning, search the internet, or retrieve CRM records by itself. The surrounding application gathers evidence and performs actions. Clef has a similar decision contract and adds multimodal inputs.

**Confidence is not a guarantee of correctness.** TypeSafe derives Choice and Score confidence from the answer’s probability distribution. Noul has no separate confidence field; its yes/no probability contains the uncertainty. A confident answer can still be wrong. Thresholds need validation for each question and model version.

Current verified documentation: [System One](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one), [Confidence](https://docs.typesafe.ai/confidence), [Clef](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/models/clef/). Publication dates for these living documentation pages are not stated; they were retrieved during the October 7 research.

### 4.1 Opportunity scoring: Autonomous Technologies

Rizwan Qaiser’s September 25, 2026 article reports an operating workflow in a Django application called Agent Rahnuma. Saved Upwork searches supply opportunities. Jev scores new opportunities before they reach Google Chat. A card shows the verdict, fit for each teammate, and the suggested reviewer. A person decides whether to bid; the described workflow does not write back to Upwork.

The five questions were:

1. Is this the agency’s kind of work?
2. Does the budget match the scope?
3. What does the client’s Upwork history show?
4. How crowded is the opportunity?
5. Should the team pursue it now, consider it, or skip it?

Each search receives its own ideal-customer description. Each teammate receives a work-profile description. Stored assessments are keyed by model and rubric so different scorers do not overwrite each other.

The database contained 68,111 jobs. The reported alignment run scored **409 jobs across three profiles: 1,227 judgments**. It cost approximately $0.08. The 68,111 figure is an inventory count, not the number verified as scored in that run.

The team compared 211 historically pursued jobs with 198 untouched jobs. The test exposed disagreements between its rubric and historical choices. Historical proposals were not a proven definition of good opportunities: none of the 211 had a Hired status in the stated historical window. The author identifies future hire-rate comparison as the next test.

Useful implementation details:

- Store the questions’ version with each result.
- Display the score where the reviewer already works.
- Inspect missed high-fit items and pursued low-fit items.
- Treat a failed API call as **no score**, not as a low score or skip.
- Compute counts, ages, and exact budget comparisons in code.

Evidence level: **practitioner-reported operating deployment**. Code, logs, and business outcomes were not independently inspected. Some historical launch/rate-limit statements in the article should not replace current official documentation.

## 5. Recommended CRM use case: grade existing contacts

The first implementation should assess contacts using the evidence already in the CRM. Name, email, and phone number alone usually do not establish customer fit or buying intent. Empty records should become **insufficient information**, not bad leads.

This section is a proposed application design based on the sources above. It has not been connected to a specific CRM.
Research record; includes historical findings, proposed designs and unresolved gaps. Read stated status.

### Inputs to read

| Input | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Contact and company facts | Evaluate documented business and role fit |
| Contact source, tags, and opportunity stage | Understand the record’s context |
| Latest inbound message and relevant recent messages | Identify current intent and objections |
| Form responses and relevant sales notes | Recover qualification facts |
| Available call transcripts | Use stated problems, commitments, and buying process |
| Approved offer, exclusions, and product facts | Provide the rubric against which to assess |
| Existing suppression, booking, and contact-status records | Let application rules decide eligibility and exact actions |

Keep known facts distinct from inferred signals. For example, a title can suggest a role, but it does not prove budget authority. Reduce unrelated conversation history before requesting a score.

Sources: [State preparation](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/state), [Jev limitations](https://docs.typesafe.ai/model-jaggedness/jev-1.13).

### Assessment fields to write

Names below are proposed CRM field names, not existing fields inspected in an account.

| Proposed field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| AI customer fit | Documented match to the defined customer profile |
| AI buying intent | Curiosity, specific problem, pricing inquiry, active evaluation, or equivalent rubric |
| AI conversation intent | Pricing, booking, product question, objection, later, not interested, unclear |
| AI missing information | Unresolved budget, authority, timing, or other qualification facts |
| AI review priority | Application-computed priority for a salesperson |

| AI model version | Model that returned the result |
| AI rubric version | Exact rules used for the assessment |

This storage design extends the practitioner’s versioned score records and TypeSafe’s structured outputs; it is a proposal rather than a vendor-required field layout.

### The contact-grading flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Read contact and relevant CRM evidence] --> B[Prepare compact state and approved rubric]
    B --> C[Jev or Clef evaluates typed questions]
    C --> D{Valid result and enough evidence?}
    D -->|No| E[Save insufficient evidence or error for review]
    D -->|Yes| F[Code combines results into review priority]
    F --> G[Save dedicated assessment fields]
    G --> H[Salesperson reviews prioritized CRM view]
```

Start with one pass through the defined contact population. Read all relevant pages rather than assuming the first returned page contains every contact. Then reassess when new evidence arrives: a reply, form response, or sales note. Use contact IDs and source-event IDs to avoid duplicate processing. Define a retry/error route so an unavailable model cannot silently downgrade a contact.

Pagination, event handling, and CRM writes depend on the actual CRM connector and must be verified when implementing. They were not executed in this research.

## 8. Adding replies later

Contact grading can run without responding to anyone. A later reply workflow would be:

**Inbound message → current CRM facts → Jev/Clef classification → handler-specific context → writing model draft → draft review → authorized delivery.**

Examples of handlers:

- Pricing: load approved pricing and package information.
- Product question: retrieve relevant product facts.
- Booking: use real calendar availability and booking rules.
- Objection: provide approved material relevant to the stated objection.
- Unclear or human requested: create a review case.
- Stop-contact request: follow the suppression route defined by application rules.

Jev selects and checks; a generative model writes. Exact prices, dates, contact eligibility, existing bookings, and side effects stay in code and source systems. An opt-out detector is an additional signal, not a substitute for existing suppression records. A false opt-out answer does not grant permission to contact a person.

This is a proposed sales adaptation of the official routing architecture and the reported outbound component, not a verified autonomous closing agent.

9. Validation before relying on CRM grades

## 9. Validation before relying on CRM grades

Use a versioned rubric and a separate human-labeled test set. Include clear fits, poor fits, missing information, ambiguous messages, objections, existing customers, explicit opt-outs, and human requests.

Check the following before grades influence actions:

- Do humans agree with the classifications?
- Which qualified contacts are being missed?
- Which poor-fit contacts rank too highly?
- Does missing information produce review rather than rejection?
- Does a failed API call produce an error/no-score state?
- Do option reordering and adversarial text change classifications?
- Do new model/rubric versions change results on the same test set?
- Can a reviewer trace each assessment to the underlying evidence?

There is no validated universal threshold such as 0.8 for this CRM use case. Choose thresholds per question using observed performance and the consequences of mistakes. Start with prioritization and review; automatic rejection needs stronger evidence than a sorting aid.

Jev’s official limitations include literal reading, numeric/date errors, option-order sensitivity, unrelated-context distraction, and susceptibility to adversarial state content. Keep arithmetic in code, write explicit criteria, and test boundary cases. Pin a model version when thresholds have been tuned against it; the `jev-latest` alias can move.

Sources: [classification evaluation cookbook](https://openrouter.ai/docs/cookbook/evaluate-and-optimize/jev-classification), [Confidence](https://docs.typesafe.ai/confidence), [Jev 1.13 limitations, reviewed October 2](https://docs.typesafe.ai/model-jaggedness/jev-1.13), [model aliases and version pinning](https://docs.typesafe.ai/models).

A proposed nurture workflow for Alex

### A proposed nurture workflow for Alex

The conversation can move among these modes rather than following an irreversible ladder:

| Mode | Intended behavior | Evidence that could justify a transition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Connect | Respond naturally to the person's actual message, including everyday topics | They introduce a relevant need or business question |
| Understand | Learn about the situation without a rapid series of qualifying questions | A clear goal, problem, or obstacle emerges |
| Help | Answer questions and provide useful, approved information | They express interest in solving the problem |
| Offer | Connect the service to the need they described | They ask about price, availability, a call, or starting |
| Follow through | Resolve remaining questions and offer a clear next step | Acceptance, deferral, decline, or need for a human |

This is a proposed application of TypeSafe's structured decision architecture, not a vendor-provided nurture algorithm. Jev could assess narrow signals; workflow rules combine the outputs; the speaking model writes the response. A friendly message alone does not establish buying intent. The agent should be able to return to helping or wait when the person changes direction.

Use approved examples of Alex's conversations to teach the speaking model how to acknowledge personal comments, handle unrelated questions, give advice, and transition toward an offer. Remember only what the contact actually shared; do not invent personal experiences or claim an internal score proves trust.

Keep the contact history in the CRM or application: stated needs, unresolved questions, timing, follow-up preferences, offers already made, objections, current mode, and the next permitted action. Retain source messages for assessments. Supply the relevant facts to Jev each time. Jev's state field is request context, not persistent customer memory.

Source and inference basis: [TypeSafe workflow design](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/how-to-build-with-system-one), [state documentation](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/state). Read October 7, 2026.

### Test complete conversations

Use saved or fictional conversations covering friendly chatter, unrelated questions, interested buyers, delays, skepticism, explicit declines, and requests for a human. Define expected behavior before testing and run multiple trials. Check whether the agent answers the actual message, remembers relevant facts, avoids premature offers, recognizes supported sales openings, respects requests to wait or stop, and makes accurate offer claims.

Keep transcripts, compare revisions against the same cases, and use human review to calibrate automatic grading. These are proposed sales-specific checks based on published evaluation guidance. Once authorized and operating, measure actual bookings and sales alongside ignored preferences and premature pitches; neither model scores nor simulated results establish business lift.

Source: [Anthropic: Demystifying evals for AI agents](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/demystifying-evals-for-ai-agents), published January 9, 2026; read October 7, 2026.

### Can Jev be fine-tuned?

No customer-specific fine-tuning or LoRA adaptation is offered in the current Jev documentation. All accounts use the same weights. Customize requests through state, instructions, criteria, examples, and downstream rules. TypeSafe says customer requests and responses are not used to train Jev.

The documentation also describes training a separate classical model on features derived from Jev probabilities. That would train a downstream predictor, not fine-tune Jev or teach it to write sales replies.

## 15. The official Hermes skill-suggestion cookbook

TypeSafe explicitly discusses Nous Research's **Hermes Agent** in its [skill-suggestion cookbook](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/skill_suggestion). This concerns the agent framework and its skill catalog; it is not an endorsement of a Hermes-branded language model as the best speaker.
Research record; includes historical findings, proposed designs and unresolved gaps. Read stated status.

### What the published implementation does

1. Load a pinned catalog of 182 Hermes skills.
2. Use one TypeSafe request to rank the skills and judge whether a skill is needed.
3. Recheck the top three candidates using fuller descriptions and instruction excerpts; reject all if none fit.
4. Add a suggestion for at most one skill to the agent's system prompt. The agent retains its own judgment and catalog.

The cookbook publishes a script and supporting-file references for this pattern. Its measured agent uses Claude Haiku 4.5 (`claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`), alongside Jev 1.12. The published run was rendered July 31, 2026; the page was read October 7, 2026. These are the experiment's pinned models, not a recommendation to use those older versions now.

| Published condition | Wrong skill loaded on covered requests | Skill loaded when none fit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Agent with catalog alone | 16.8% | 9.8% |
| Agent with TypeSafe suggestion | 7.3% | 4.0% |
| Agent given the correct answer | 2.5% | 1.2% |

The evaluation covers 488 single-turn requests: 315 with a matching skill and 173 with no matching skill. The page says covered requests were generated from the skills by Claude Sonnet 5. This is a vendor-published skill-selection experiment, not a multi-turn sales test, independently reproduced result, or proof of a complete Hermes runtime integration in Alex's environment. Even the correct-answer condition still has errors.

### How the pattern could apply to Alex's sales agent

A proposed sales catalog could include skills for understanding a need, answering an objection, sharing approved information, continuing nurture, offering a call, and honoring a requested pause. Jev could help select a relevant skill—or select none—before the speaking model responds. Each skill would contain approved behavior and examples. Workflow rules would still control customer contact and CRM actions.

That application is an inference from the cookbook architecture. The source does not demonstrate sales conversions, natural conversation quality, or a ready-made sales skill library. Validate the conversation modes and skill selection on the multi-turn tests above before considering live use.
